paper_metadata.title: Flow Behavior and Microstructure of Hot-Worked TiNbTaVW Refractory High-Entropy Alloy

evidence.quote: In the TiNbTaVW RHEA, serrations were seen in both the elastic and plastic regions.
This was compared with a commercial-grade nickel-based superalloy, IN718.

evidence.section: 5. Experimental Section
evidence.quote: The TiNbTaVW RHEA was produced through vacuum arc melting under ultrahigh-purity argon gas on a water-cooled copper hearth to obtain an arc-melted alloy.

evidence.section: 5. Experimental Section
evidence.quote: Additionally, a nickel-based IN718 superalloy was acquired.

evidence.section: 5. Experimental Section
evidence.quote: The TiNbTaVW RHEA was produced through vacuum arc melting under ultrahigh-purity argon gas on a water-cooled copper hearth to obtain an arc-melted alloy. The RHEA was produced using commercial high-purity raw elemental powders comprising Ti (99.7 wt% purity), Nb (99.9 wt% purity), V (99.9 wt% purity), Ta (99.95 wt% purity), and W (99.9 wt% purity)... The TiNbTaVW samples were flipped and remelted three times to ensure chemical homogeneity.

evidence.section: 5. Experimental Section
evidence.quote: For each test, the samples were heated to a set deformation temperature of 950, 1000, and 1050 °C at a heating rate of 5 °C s-1 and held at this temperature for 180 s to ensure homogenization before compression.

evidence.section: 5. Experimental Section
evidence.quote: The samples were deformed at a strain rate of 10-3 s-1 and a total strain of 0.1, followed by air cooling to retain the microstructure.

evidence.section: 4. Conclusion
evidence.quote: The TiNbTaVW RHEA has higher-temperature strengths of 910, 870, and 658 MPa, compared to the IN718 alloy, with 72, 87, and 61 MPa at 950, 1000, and 1050 °C/10-3 s-1, respectively.
